summary:
Radar for 2026-11-04 (GLP-1 focus). I checked 11 leads. The best early opportunity is a new body-worry topic: nail changes on GLP-1 medicines. The Dermatology Digest covered it today, the study came out Oct 1 (Healio and HCPLive), and there is still little creator coverage. It fits our best Short format, "Is this normal?" with tirzepatide in the title, and it pairs with the live Hair Loss long-form. One rule for every script: the study covers GLP-1 users as a class, so scripts must not credit the finding to tirzepatide alone.

Lane A long-form backlog, still the top earners: injection site reactions (the Short hit 223 views by day 2), fatigue, birth control (label only), and dehydration/sick days.

Seasonal hooks gaining speed:
- **Thanksgiving:** seen in 9 snapshots, momentum rising 78 → 83, peak Nov 18–27.
- **Cold and flu sick days:** new and seasonal.
- **Social eating when you get full fast:** today's Sun Sentinel advice column about GLP-1 users who "eat so fast" gives a ready-made Lane A question about eating out.

News hooks:
- A new target trial emulation (Diabetes Obes Metab, Nov 3) looked at semaglutide, tirzepatide and alcohol-related outcomes. With EMJ coverage it refreshes the holiday-drinking question, but the data are observational.
- The Bone meta-analysis (Nov 2) and Medscape's "not linked to fracture risk" story give a funnel Short into Bones & Muscle.
- ObesityWeek (Nov 14–17) should bring full REDEFINE 4 results (CagriSema vs tirzepatide), which is our only realistic head-to-head long-form trigger.

Peaking, so differentiated angles only:
- The AHA prediabetes study (observational; covered by HealthDay, US News and Reuters, and our own S2 already shipped).
- Novo's Q3 report and the Wegovy pill's Australian approval (TGA). This is mostly business news. The useful angle for AU viewers is pill vs injection.

Old stories being reshared:
- Hormone therapy plus tirzepatide (Mayo study from January; Newsweek reran it Nov 3).
- The heat and dehydration warnings (from July).
- Stanford's "natural Ozempic" (animal data, first reported in July).

Don't call any of these new. Only the hormone therapy story is worth a cautious Short.

Rejected: the "natural GLP-1 alternatives" supplement listicles, retatrutide "supplier" and research-chemical pieces, $99 telehealth ads, and the "natural Ozempic" story used as a buyable fix.

Sources: [Healio nail study](https://www.healio.com/news/dermatology/20261002/glp1-use-associated-with-nail-detachment-hair-loss), [HCPLive](https://hcplive.com/view/nail-detachment-4-times-more-common-with-glp-1-use), [Mayo HT + tirzepatide](https://www.news-medical.net/news/20260122/Menopausal-hormone-therapy-linked-to-greater-weight-loss-with-tirzepatide.aspx), [Poison center data](https://www.drugtopics.com/view/data-show-rise-in-glp-1-poison-center-calls-tied-to-dosing-errors), [Stanford BRP](https://sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/07/260719230608.htm), [Fracture studies](https://www.technologynetworks.com/biopharma/news/do-glp-1-drugs-increase-fracture-risk-415323), [Heat warnings](https://www.goodmorningamerica.com/wellness/story/amid-heat-wave-doctors-warn-health-risks-people-134556097), [Alcohol TTE](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC12673470/).

candidates.topic: Nail changes on GLP-1 medicines (nail lifting, discoloration): is it normal on tirzepatide? Survey study: nail detachment 39% of GLP-1 users vs 9% of non-users; still about 2–3× more common after adjusting for skin conditions and nutrient deficiencies; the link nearly disappeared when only counting problems that started after treatment
candidates.angle: A calm 'Is this normal?' Short with tirzepatide in the title (e.g. 'Tirzepatide and Nail Changes: Is This Normal?'), but say clearly that the study looked at GLP-1 medicines as a group. Give the honest numbers plus the caveat (about half of users already had nail problems before starting). Possible connections people ask about (eating less, fast weight loss) are hypotheses, not findings. Say when to see a doctor or dermatologist. A companion to the live Hair Loss long-form; put its link on line 1 of the description.
keywords: is nail damage from mounjaro normal
candidates.why_now: Dermatology Digest covered it today (Nov 4) after the Oct 1 study (Healio, HCPLive, Gizmodo's 'hair loss was just the start'). It is spreading from derm news into consumer press, and there is little creator coverage yet. It sits right next to our 1,015-view hair Short, and body-worry Shorts are our proven best format.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 use associated with nail detachment and hair loss
Nail detachment about 4× more common with GLP-1 use; caveats on pre-existing problems
GLP-1 users report fingernail detachment
GLP-1 RA Use and Nail Detachment: What's the Connection?

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide injection site reactions: what's normal (redness, itching, small lumps), what the label reports, and when to call your prescriber
candidates.angle: The next Lane A long-form. The first sentence answers 'Is this normal?'. Cover what the label reports and the mild, short-lived reactions people commonly describe. Infection warning signs are our own safety lines (no source tag). Use the prescriber line. No technique-as-dosing advice beyond 'follow your pen's instructions and ask your pharmacist'.
candidates.predicted_peak: evergreen; search grows with every new starter
candidates.why_now: Seen in 7 snapshots, momentum rising 72 → 76. Its Short reached 223 views by day 2, our best start since the hair Short. It answers a question no live Lane A video covers.

evidence.signal: Seen 7×, momentum 72 → 76
Injection-site Short 223 views by day 2; listed as a priority Lane A topic

candidates.topic: Thanksgiving on tirzepatide: feeling full fast, protein first, smaller plates, eating slower, alcohol and easing nausea at a big holiday meal
candidates.angle: The long-form is already live. Run 20:00 funnel Shorts with fresh questions ('Why do I get full after 3 bites on tirzepatide?', 'Is it OK to leave food on my plate?'), each pointing to the Thanksgiving long-form. Use the joint GLP-1 nutrition advisory wording exactly.
candidates.why_now: Seen in 9 snapshots, rising 78 → 83. It is a fixed seasonal peak 2–3 weeks away, and food-press stories on how GLP-1 users are 'redefining indulgence' are growing (FoodNavigator, Nov 4).

evidence.signal: How are GLP-1 users redefining indulgence?
Seen 9×, momentum 78 → 83

candidates.topic: Eating out and social dinners on tirzepatide: getting full fast, eating slowly, ordering smaller, and not feeling awkward at the table
candidates.angle: A new Lane A question next to What to Eat: 'Tirzepatide at Restaurants: How to Order?' (≤50 characters). Cover practical habits (protein-first orders, starters as mains, boxing leftovers, pacing, the 'I'm full' script) plus why getting full early happens (slower stomach emptying). Positive framing; no restriction messaging. The Sun Sentinel advice letter is the 'you' scenario.
keywords: full after a few bites mounjaro
candidates.why_now: Today's Sun Sentinel 'Asking Eric' advice letter ('The GLP-1 women eat so fast that our dinners are no fun') shows the social side of GLP-1 reaching mainstream advice columns, just as holiday parties and restaurant meals start. Few creators answer it practically.

evidence.signal: Asking Eric: The GLP-1 women eat so fast that our dinners are no fun
GLP-1 users redefining indulgence

candidates.topic: Why am I so tired on tirzepatide? Zepbound label fatigue 5% (5 mg), 6% (10 mg), 7% (15 mg) vs 3% on placebo
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form. The first sentence answers the title using the label rates. Possible everyday drivers (eating much less, too little fluid, nausea, sleep) are framed as possibilities, not findings. Cover what helps (protein, hydration, sleep, movement) and when to call the prescriber. Dark winter mornings make a good 'you' scenario.
keywords: why am i so tired on mounjaro
candidates.why_now: Seen in 5+ snapshots at 80–82 momentum, and it's a named priority in this week's playbook. Shorter days in November raise 'tired' searches.

evidence.signal: Seen 5×, momentum 80–82

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide when you're sick this cold and flu season: staying hydrated when you can't eat, the label's kidney/dehydration warning, and checking with a pharmacist before cold remedies
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form: 'Tirzepatide and a Stomach Bug: What to Know' or 'Sick on Tirzepatide?'. Cover hydration signs, the label's acute kidney injury warning (dehydration from vomiting or diarrhoea), and when to call the prescriber. Strictly no 'skip a dose' or dose advice: 'ask your prescriber what to do with your medicine when you're sick.' This merges the dehydration Lane A topic with the seasonal hook.
keywords: can I take cold medicine with mounjaro
candidates.why_now: Flu season is starting. ABC reshared its GLP-1 dehydration story today (it first ran in July), and the dehydration topic has held 70–74 across 5 snapshots. Few creators combine 'sick day' and GLP-1.

evidence.signal: Doctors warn of GLP-1 dehydration risks (first published July 2026, resurfaced Nov 4)
Doctors warn GLP-1 users about dehydration risk
Cold and flu season on tirzepatide (Yahoo Health, Oct 31), momentum 78

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and birth control pills: what the label says about reduced oral contraceptive exposure, refreshed by the GLP-1/GIP pregnancy-outcomes meta-analysis (Front Pharmacol, Oct 16)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form, label only. Explain why gastric emptying matters for pills and what the label says around starting and dose increases, with no instructions. Send viewers to their prescriber. The pregnancy meta-analysis appears only as context (time-window stratified; observational).
keywords: does mounjaro make birth control less effective
candidates.why_now: Seen in 4 snapshots (73–76) and listed third in this week's Lane A order. It's a high-intent question for women 25–45 with few clear answers on YouTube.

evidence.signal: Pregnancy and perinatal outcomes after GLP-1 and dual GLP-1/GIP exposure: meta-analysis

candidates.topic: Does tirzepatide change how alcohol feels? New target trial emulation of semaglutide, tirzepatide and recorded alcohol-related outcomes in type 2 diabetes (Diabetes Obes Metab, Nov 3) plus EMJ 'GLP-1 RAs cut alcohol cravings' (Nov 4)
candidates.angle: A 13:00 Short timed for holiday party season. Say what the research shows: observational, so 'linked to', not 'causes'. Note the T2D population, that randomized trials are ongoing, and that the medicine isn't approved for alcohol use disorder. Add a practical line: alcohol can add to stomach side effects and dehydration, so ask your prescriber.
candidates.why_now: A fresh Nov 3 paper plus EMJ coverage today, building on last week's beer-sales and Medscape stories (seen in 2 snapshots). Holiday drinking questions peak in December.

evidence.signal: Semaglutide, tirzepatide and clinically recorded alcohol-related outcomes in T2D: target trial emulation
Earlier TTE: tirzepatide and semaglutide linked to lower incident AUD vs DPP-4 inhibitors
GLP-1 receptor agonists cut alcohol cravings

candidates.topic: ObesityWeek 2026 (Nov 14–17): full REDEFINE 4 results, CagriSema vs tirzepatide in adults with obesity (open-label, 84 weeks; topline about 23% with CagriSema, non-inferiority to tirzepatide not met)
candidates.angle: Prepare a 13:00 Short 'Tirzepatide vs CagriSema: What the Full Data Show' for the day the full results go public. If it's a randomized head-to-head released within 48 h, it qualifies as an extra L2 long-form under the playbook. Name tirzepatide first, state the population, call it open-label, and include the 'don't switch' line.
candidates.why_now: A scheduled catalyst 10 days out. Tirzepatide-first head-to-heads in obesity populations reach 107–174 views for us. Novo's Q3 news today puts its pipeline (zenagamtide, CagriSema) back in the headlines.

evidence.signal: Novo puts zenagamtide to decisive test as semaglutide successor
ObesityWeek / REDEFINE 4 watch seen 2×, momentum 78

candidates.topic: Do GLP-1 medicines weaken bones? New meta-analysis of placebo-controlled RCTs on bone metabolism (Bone, Nov 2; mostly first-generation agents) plus Medscape 'GLP-1 therapies not linked to increased fracture risk in three studies' (Nov 2)
candidates.angle: A 20:00 funnel Short to the live Bones & Muscle long-form: 'Will tirzepatide weaken my bones?'. Give the honest answer: mixed observational evidence, with some studies lower and one JCEM study modestly higher. The RCT meta-analysis mostly covers older GLP-1 drugs, so it shouldn't be credited to tirzepatide. Strength training and protein are what help. Class wording throughout.
candidates.why_now: Two fresh items (Bone meta-analysis Nov 2, Medscape Nov 2) plus a 1-snapshot falls/fracture topic. Bones & Muscle holds 80% AVD but gets only about 177 impressions, so it needs funnel traffic.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 RAs and bone metabolism: SR/MA of placebo-controlled RCTs (predominantly first-generation)
Do GLP-1 drugs increase fracture risk? (conflicting observational results)
GLP-1s may reduce fracture risk in obesity/T2D

candidates.topic: What happens after you stop: GLP-1 aftercare and staying on track (EMJ 'GLP-1 aftercare neglected despite weight regain risk', Nov 4; Amgen 'gap between prescriptions and persistence', Nov 4), anchored on SURMOUNT-4
candidates.angle: Funnel Shorts to the stopping long-form shipped 11-04, using a new fact each time (e.g. placebo still ended 9.9% below its starting weight on average in SURMOUNT-4, no diabetes). Keep it positive: plan with your prescriber, and protein and strength habits matter. Include 'don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own'.
keywords: what happens when you stop mounjaro
candidates.why_now: Seen in 9 snapshots in total (84–88), with two new industry and expert pieces today about persistence and aftercare. The New Year resolution cycle is coming.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 aftercare neglected despite weight regain risk
Early treatment trajectory and long-term persistence to semaglutide

candidates.topic: Menopause hormone therapy and tirzepatide: Mayo Clinic records study (120 postmenopausal women; 19.2% vs 14.0% mean weight loss; observational), reshared by Newsweek Nov 3
candidates.angle: A 13:00 Short for women 45–65: 'Tirzepatide and HRT: Does It Change Results?'. Give the honest answer: an association in a small, non-randomized study, with a randomized trial planned. Don't call it new (published January 2026). Don't suggest starting HRT to boost weight loss; talk to your clinician.
candidates.why_now: Newsweek's Nov 3 reshare is pushing the story to a big audience of midlife women who already search 'Mounjaro menopause'. It fits our audience well.

evidence.signal: Menopausal hormone therapy linked to greater weight loss with tirzepatide
Hormone therapy linked to how some women respond to GLP-1 drugs

candidates.topic: Wegovy pill approved in Australia (TGA, Nov 3–4) as Novo raises its outlook on oral demand: how a daily GLP-1 pill compares with weekly injections
candidates.angle: A Short or Reel for AU and UK viewers: 'GLP-1 Pill vs Injection: What's Different?'. Cover daily vs weekly dosing routines in general terms (no dose instructions), why oral doses are higher (absorption), and what the trials show, citing separate trials, not head-to-head. Avoid an 'Approved yet?' title and a brand-first title.

evidence.signal: Australia's first GLP-1 weight-loss pill approved; how it differs from injections

candidates.angle: Only with a new angle, since S2 11-04 already covered it. Option: 'Prediabetes on tirzepatide: what SURMOUNT-1's 3-year data showed' (randomized). Say GLP-1s aren't approved for diabetes prevention alone. Class wording for the AHA study.

candidates.angle: A 13:00 'what's confirmed?' Short with a loop ending. Retatrutide is still in Phase 3 and not approved anywhere, and products sold online aren't the trial drug. Point to the real Phase 3 data (TRIUMPH sleep apnea, NEJM Oct 20). Counts as the week's single gray-market Short. Name no sellers.

10k doses of smuggled 'Godzilla' fat jabs seized at UK borders
Compounding Oversight Bill advances amid FDA warnings on unapproved retatrutide

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines after 65 and with frailty: JAMA analysis (Oct 30), the Diabetes Obes Metab cardiovascular meta-analysis by age group (Oct 27), and the EMA age-stratified evidence gap review (Front Pharmacol, Oct 20)
candidates.angle: An 08:00 reassurance Short: 'Tirzepatide After 65: Is It Safe?'. Give the honest answer: benefits seen across age groups in RCTs, older adults are under-represented, and muscle and bone protection matter (protein, strength). Keep class claims class-level. Point to the prescriber and to Bones & Muscle.
candidates.why_now: Three fresh papers in 2 weeks. US Medicare open enrolment runs now, so older adults are researching (topic only; no cost angle).

evidence.signal: Analysis asks: are GLP-1 drugs safe in people with frailty?
CV effects of GLP-1 RAs across age groups: updated meta-analysis of RCTs
Age-stratified evidence availability in EMA reports

candidates.topic: Accidental extra dose: GLP-1 poison-center calls doubled in Washington (KIRO, Nov 4); most were therapeutic errors (daily instead of weekly, unit confusion with compounded vials)
candidates.angle: Safety Short only: 'Took an Extra Tirzepatide Dose by Mistake?'. Say what to do: call Poison Control (US 1-800-222-1222) or your prescriber and watch for severe nausea or vomiting. Use your approved pen as prescribed and ask the pharmacist if anything is unclear. No dose numbers, no unit conversions, and no naming or endorsing compounded products.
candidates.why_now: The local TV story today follows national poison-center data (Drug Topics, July). People search it in a panic, and the honest answer is short and protective.

evidence.signal: Rise in GLP-1 poison center calls tied to dosing errors
GLP-1 poison calls double in Washington

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines and the eyes: J Korean Med Sci review of ocular safety and retinal outcomes (Nov 2)
candidates.angle: A cautious 08:00 Short, 'Tirzepatide and Your Eyes: What's Known?', only if the fact-checker can anchor every claim (rare NAION signal from observational data, label retinopathy note in T2D). Class wording, calm mascot, and see an eye doctor urgently for sudden vision loss.
candidates.why_now: A fresh review, and eye side effects keep resurfacing as a search worry. Low competition, but the evidence is nuanced.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 RAs and the eye: ocular safety, retinal outcomes
